_comment: Every change to the learning content, dated — including the ones that make us look bad. A lesson that was wrong is more useful to a learner as a published correction than as a quiet edit. Hand-maintained on purpose: git history records what changed, not why it mattered or who caught it. Newest first. 'kind' must be one of the values scripts/validate-content.mjs allows.

entries.what: AI as an Assistive Tool published — eight lessons on reading, writing, seeing, hearing, focus and communication when those are barriers, plus how to make things other people can actually get at. Written after an audit found the curriculum had no coverage of assistive use at all.

Advanced Prompting published — the first Practitioner module. Eight lessons on few-shot examples, structured output, splitting a prompt into single-purpose steps, chaining without compounding errors, persistent instructions, long inputs, testing a prompt against a saved evaluation set, and building prompts that survive a model update.

AI Ethics & Responsible Use published — eight lessons on authorship, disclosing AI use, where bias comes from and lands, who answers when something goes wrong, the environmental and labour costs, automating work that belongs to colleagues, how to refuse, and writing your own code of conduct. This completes the Explorer track: 64 lessons across eight modules.

Truth, Verification & Critical Thinking published — eight lessons on why fluency defeats scepticism, triaging which claims to check, a two-minute verification method, judging sources, handling disagreement, how manipulation finds you, your own bias, and a habit small enough to survive. This module is compulsory for certification.

Creative AI: Image, Video & Voice published — eight lessons on how diffusion models actually work, describing an image, iterating with seeds, the artist-style question, the current limits of video, voice cloning and consent, labelling what you made, and the categories that are not grey areas.

Documents, Spreadsheets & Presentations published — eight lessons on outlining before prose, drafting in your own voice, using an assistant as a critic, spreadsheet formulas you can test, recomputing every number, assertion-headline slides, rewriting for a different reader, and the final consistency pass.

Everyday Productivity published — eight lessons on where AI actually fits in your day, email, reading long documents, research that cites its sources, meeting notes, planning, a twenty-minute routine, and what not to hand over.
Reading preferences added: text size, line spacing, line length, contrast, a reading typeface and data saver. Dark mode also now follows your device — it had been built but never switched on.
Answer options are now shuffled. 94% of correct answers had been sitting in the middle slot, so always picking the middle passed every module quiz without reading the question.
Eight lessons on briefing, iteration, correcting a wrong answer, and the requests no wording can rescue. Adds a 22-question quiz bank and 24 review cards.
NotebookLM was renamed Gemini Notebook by Google in July. The lesson title and the tool card now say so, and the documentation link it pointed at had been dead for six weeks.
Claude's tool card claimed no voice support. Voice mode has shipped on every plan, so the capability grid was showing learners a wrong fact.
